Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Case called out in the revised list.
No one appears on behalf of the revisionist to press this criminal revision.
Learned A.G.A. representing the State is present.

2. The present criminal revision has been filed challenging the judgement and order dated 21.2.2003 passed by Sri Sanjay Shankar Pandey, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 12, Jaunpur,
in Complaint Case No. 1070 of 1999 (State of U.P. Vs. Om Prakash Singh), under sections 16 (1) (a)
(i) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and accordingly sentenced to one year rigorous imprisonment along with a fine of Rs.1000/-.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 12, Jaunpur
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Complaint Case No. 1070 of 1999 (State of U.P. Vs. Om Prakash Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Upon failure to deposit the fine, the accused is to undergo 1 month additional imprisonment.
3. Feeling aggrieved by the order dated 21.2.2003, the revisionist filed an appeal before the Additional Sessions Judge, Jaunpur.

The same was registered as Appeal No. 24 of 2003 (Om Om Prakash Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191136501/
1 Prakash Singh Vs. State).

entities.text: Om Om Prakash Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appellate Court dismissed the appeal filed by the revisionist.
Consequence of the same is that the judgement and order dated 21.3.2003 passed by the Trial Court stood confirmed.
4. I have perused the judgements passed by Trial Court as well as Appellate Court.

5. Trial Court has recorded an specific finding holding that sample of milk collected from the revisionist showed adulteration of carbonate neutralizer, the use of which is prohibited for mixing it with milk.
As such, the product sold by the revisionist falls within the category of adulterated food product.
The aforesaid finding, which has been recorded by the Trial Court, has also been confirmed by the Appellate Court.
6. The judicial review in exercise of revisional jurisdiction is not like an appeal.

It is a supervisory jurisdiction which is exercised by the Court to correct the manifest error in the orders of subordinate courts but should not be exercised in a manner so as to turn the Revisional court in a Court of Appeal.
The legislature has differently made provisions for appeal and revision and the distinction of two jurisdictions has to be maintained.

7. Construing old Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1898, pertaining to revisional jurisdiction, the Court in D. Stephens Vs. Nosibolla, AIR 1951 SC 196 said that revisional jurisdiction under Section 439 of the Code ought not to be exercised lightly particularly when it is invoked by private complainant against an order of acquittal which could have been appealed against by the Government under Section 417.

entities.text: D. Stephens Vs. Nosibolla, AIR 1951 SC 196
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It could be exercised only in exceptional cases where the interests of public justice require interference for the correction of a manifest illegality, or the prevention of a gross miscarriage of justice.
In other words, the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court cannot be invoked merely because the lower court has taken a wrong view of law or misappreciated the evidence on record.

8. In K. Chinnaswamy Reddy Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 1962 SC 1788 it was held that revisional jurisdiction should be exercised by the High Court in exceptional cases only when there is some glaring defect in the procedure or a manifest error on a point of law resulting in flagrant miscarriage of justice.

entities.text: K. Chinnaswamy Reddy Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 1962 SC 1788
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, this was also a case in which revisional jurisdiction was invoked against an order of acquittal.

If the Court lacks jurisdiction or has excluded evidence which was admissible or relied on inadmissible evidence or material evidence has been overlooked etc., then only this Court would be justified in exercising revisional power and not otherwise.

9. The above view has been reiterated in Mahendra Pratap Singh Vs. Sarju Singh, AIR 1968 SC 707;
Khetrabasi Samal Vs. State of Orissa, AIR 1970 SC 272; Satyendra Nath Dutta and another Vs. Ram Narain, AIR 1975 SC 580; Jagannath Choudhary and others Vs. Ramayan Singh and another,
2002(5) SCC 659; and, Johar and others Vs. Mandal Prasad and another, 2008 Cr.L.J. 1627 (S.C.).
10.

entities.text: Duli Chand Vs. Delhi Administration, 1975(4) SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

2 refusing to re-appreciate evidence for determining whether the concurrent findings of fact reached by learned Magistrate and Sessions Judge was correct.

11. In Pathumma and another Vs. Muhammad, 1986(2) SCC 585 reiterating the above view the Court said that in revisional jurisdiction the High Court would not be justified in substituting its own view for that of a Magistrate on a question of fact.

entities.text: Pathumma and another Vs. Muhammad, 1986(2) SCC 585
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. In Munna Devi Vs. State of Rajasthan and another, 2001(9) SCC 631 the Court said:
"The revision power under the Code of Criminal procedure cannot be exercised in a routine and casual manner.

entities.text: Munna Devi Vs. State of Rajasthan and another, 2001(9) SCC 631
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While exercising such powers the High Court has no authority to appreciate the evidence in the manner as the trial and the appellate courts are required to do.

Revisional powers could be exercised only when it is shown that there is a legal bar against the continuance of the criminal proceedings or the framing of charge or the facts as stated in the First Information Report even if they are taken at the face value and accepted in their entirety do not constitute the offence for which the accused has been charged."
13.

In Ram Briksh Singh and others Vs. Ambika Yadav and another, 2004(7) SCC 665, in a matter again arising from the judgment of acquittal, the revisional power of High Court was examined and the Court said:
"4. Sections 397 to 401 of the Code are group of sections conferring higher and superior courts a sort of supervisory jurisdiction.

entities.text: Ram Briksh Singh and others Vs. Ambika Yadav and another, 2004(7) SCC 665
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These powers are required to be exercised sparingly.

Though the jurisdiction under Section 401 cannot be invoked to only correct wrong appreciation of evidence and the High Court is not required to act as a court of appeal but at the same time, it is the duty of the court to correct manifest illegality resulting in gross miscarriage of justice."

14. In absence of anything to show as to what evidence has not been examined or the finding of fact recorded by Court below as noted above is perverse or contrary to material on record, no interference is called for.
15. In view of above, revision lacks merit.
Dismissed.
16. Certify this judgment to the lower court immediately.
